title: Portfolio Threads: Vision Map — Lexi Barnes
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight personal "portfolio threads" tracker — one-page view for the quarter that ties small outcome bets together. Not an official OKR doc, but a working scratch that helps me prioritize weekly check-ins and triage tradeoffs across engineering, writing, and mentoring work.

High-level north star for the quarter:
- Move from "visibility" to "reliability": ship durable onboarding materials + two small infra improvements that reduce triaged incidents. Personal measure: at least one infra change merged that cuts mean page load or debug time by ~15% for the dev harness.

Portfolio threads (3 linked bets) — why these three?
1) Developer onboarding narrative (writing + playbook) — confidence bet
   - Why: reduce time-to-first-success for new hires and customer POCs.
   - Outcome target: publish a single, opinionated onboarding doc + one example repo that gets reused in onboarding calls. Measure: 4 new devs can run the sample stack end-to-end within 90 minutes (goal).
   - Key actions: draft outline, record 20-min walkthrough video, iterate after first hire onboarding, land in docs repo (PR referenced above).

2) Lightweight infra reliability improvements — leverage small wins
   - Why: cumulative small fixes reduce context-switch overhead for SREs and reduce noisy alerts.
   - Outcome target: land 2 changes (e.g., better healthcheck, guardrail for stale cache) that lower op-hours spent on the dev harness by ~10% per week.
   - Key actions: scope fix for cache eviction (ENG-4321), add better retry/backoff logic in local dev runner, add a simple smoke test.

3) Mentorship & craft time — grow two engineers and ship thinking pieces
   - Why: enable multiplier effect and make knowledge accessible.
   - Outcome target: one mentee promoted or owning a cross-team project; write one long-form doc on "private deployment onboarding patterns" and circulate.
   - Key actions: weekly 1:1s with Mentee A, run a brown-bag on testing strategies, draft doc and solicit feedback from Aisha and Miguel.

Signal measures (personal, not product metrics)
- Weekly slots blocked for "deep work": 6 x 2-hour blocks / bi-weekly (target achieved: 9/12 this month).
- Draft docs produced: 3 (outline, first draft, peer-reviewed draft).
- Mentee checkpoints: biweekly learning plan updates (3/3 completed).
- Incidents reduced on dev harness: anecdotal improvement; need to instrument properly.

Mini-experiments to run
- A: 90-minute onboarding checklist — trial with new hire and collect time-to-run metrics.
- B: Smoke test as pre-merge job — run on small PR sample, measure false positives/negatives.
- C: Office hours June — run three drop-in sessions for new hires/users, log common pain points.

Triage & prioritization guidance (for me)
- If a request blocks >1 person from onboarding: top priority.
- If a change reduces repeated manual steps (repro steps >3 times/week): high priority.
- Otherwise, batch with writing tasks if it takes <2 hours to complete.

Open questions / unknowns
- What baseline metric should I use to claim the dev harness is "faster"? (p50 dev task time? # of commands to repro?)
- How should I instrument anecdotal reliability improvements to show impact to SRE/product?
- Is the onboarding doc single source of truth or a complementary quickstart + deep-dive?

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: scope creep on onboarding doc. Mitigation: ship minimal quickstart first (MVP).
- Risk: infra fixes get deprioritized by urgent ticket churn. Mitigation: tag fixes with "onboarding-critical" and sync with SRE owner weekly.
- Risk: mentorship bandwidth mismatch. Mitigation: recalibrate scope and set explicit 8-week deliverables with mentee.

Next 2-week check-ins (concrete)
- Week 1: finish onboarding outline; record walkthrough draft; open PR for docs repo.
- Week 2: land cache eviction PR; run first smoke test on main; capture before/after timings.
- End of 2 weeks: 30-min retrospective with Aisha + Miguel to review progress and blockers.

Notes to self (style / process observations)
- Prefer checklists labeled "MVP" vs "deluxe" to avoid overdesign.
- Use video clips (short) to capture flow; they convert better in onboarding than long text alone.
- Keep a single small spreadsheet for measurement — start with just two columns: "task" + "time-to-complete".

Actionable TODO (short)
- [ ] Outline doc in repo (due: 2026-02-25).
- [ ] Record 20m walkthrough (due: 2026-03-01).
- [ ] Open PR for cache eviction change (ENG-4321) and add smoke test (due: 2026-02-28).
- [ ] Schedule brown-bag for testing strategies (target week of 2026-03-08).

Quick retrospective (end of last quarter)
- Wins: shipped a small debug helper that saved ~30 minutes/week across the oncall rotation; mentee ran first oncall shift with confidence.
- Misses: delayed the longer onboarding narrative, got stuck in perfection loop.
- Learnings: ship pragmatic artifacts early, instrument simple metrics, lean on peers for feedback.

References / links to backfill later:
- Confluence draft: private-deployments onboarding (linked above).
- Related PR for devx-hub: PR#678 (linked above).
- Slack thread with feedback from hiring manager: link above.

If I only do one thing this week:
- Ship the quickstart that makes a new engineer run the sample end-to-end once without me on call.

End.
